newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi typhus epidemic is worst since 1945 - WHO.
newsitem.headline: Burundi typhus epidemic is worst since 1945 - WHO.

text.p: The world's worst typhus outbreak since World War Two has infected thousands of people in Burundi, the U.N. World Health Organisation (WHO) said on Monday.
Some 20,000 typhus cases were reported between January and March in three northwest provinces hit by civil war, WHO said.
The epidemic is concentrated in what are officially called "regroupment camps" for villagers guarded by the Tutsi-dominated army to deny access to Hutu rebels but it has spread to other settlements.
WHO's Burundi representative Bernard Lala said in a report that exact mortality rates were impossible to determine but between one and 20 percent of those infected had died.
"The outbreak of the disease in Burundi is the most severe typhus epidemic in the world since the Second World War," WHO said.

More than 300 cases were arriving at Kayanza hospital each week, according to state-run Burundian television, and cases of the fever, which produces spots and abdominal pain, have also been detected in rural Bujumbura province's Mutumba commune.
"It's a sickness that always comes in the wake of war. It is passed by skin lice and its spread is accelerated by the close proximity of people in the camps," Lala said.
"We must...attack the roots of the disease with pesticides to avert the spread of the epidemic," he added.
WHO conducted seminars in April to educate public health workers on detecting typhus cases and monitoring their spread.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi in civil war between the army and Hutu rebels and massacres since the country's first elected Hutu president was killed by Tutsi troops in 1993.
